title: add tokenization-robustness-evaluator-and-ci-gate
author: Aisha Raman
release_notes: Adds a tokenization robustness CI gate that runs prompt normalization permutations and fails when semantic divergence exceeds threshold. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation:
We observed intermittent, low-frequency regressions that only surface when prompt normalization or tokenizer behavior changes (e.g. updated tokenizers, unicode normalization, whitespace trimming). These regressions are noisy and hard to reproduce locally because they depend on tiny tokenization variants. This PR introduces a tokenization robustness evaluator and a CI gate that runs a small matrix of prompt-normalization variants against a reference prompt-set and flags semantic regressions above configured thresholds.

What this PR does (high-level):
- New evaluator: tokenization_robustness.py that produces per-prompt divergence scores across a set of normalization strategies (NFC/NFKC, collapse-whitespace, preserve-newline, strip-zero-width, explicit-space-escape). Divergence is computed with a composite metric (semantic-similarity cosine on sentence-bert embeddings + normalized edit distance).
- CI hook: a new GitHub Actions job (tokenization-robustness-check) wired into the eval-harness CI matrix. The job runs fast-mode (sampled 250 prompts) by default; full-mode (all prompts) can be enabled via a label.
- Config: tokenization_gate.yaml added to allow per-prompt-set thresholds, severity (warn/fail), and fallback policy (accept-if-high-confidence).
- Reporting: artifacts include an HTML summary (tokenization_robustness_report.html) and a compact JSON that CI consumes to decide pass/fail. The report includes top-10 worst regressions with tokenization diff snippets.
- Tests: adds unit tests and a small integration smoke test that simulates a tokenizer drift by toggling NFKC normalization.

Checklist:
- [x] evaluator implementation with vectorized similarity calculation
- [x] CI action and workflow changes
- [x] config schema and default thresholds
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] changelog / release note entry

Why this is different from existing eval gates:
Existing gates focus on prompt drift, paraphrase probing, and perturbation fuzzing. This gate explicitly targets sensitivity introduced by tokenization and normalization layers (e.g., encoder updates, platform language packs). It accommodates deterministic token-level diffs and semantic-level comparisons and provides an explainable HTML artifact that surfaces tokenization differences side-by-side with model outputs.

Operational notes:
- Default mode is non-blocking for existing prompt-sets (severity: warn). After a two-week observation window we'll toggle the default to fail for high-impact prompt-sets.
- Running full-mode increases CI time by ~12 minutes; kept optional via label to avoid CI slowdowns on small PRs.
- The evaluator uses a cached embedding model for speed; CI job uses a tiny distilled embedder to remain cost-effective.

Related work:
- ENG-2213: investigation into flaky regressions tied to tokenizer bump
- ENG-2214: RFC on normalization policy across SDKs

Merge outcome:
Squash-merged into main after a follow-up patch (see commits) to tighten thresholds based on initial run data.

review_comments: Marco Gutierrez: Nice approach. Can you clarify the composite metric weighting and how that interacts with short prompts? Short prompts tend to inflate edit distance; consider length-normalized thresholds.
Aisha Raman: Good point — I added length normalization and a tunable weight in tokenization_gate.yaml. See commit 'Adjust thresholds after initial CI run'.
Priya Bhattacharya: CI cost looks reasonable, but we should avoid running full-mode on every push. Can we gate full-mode behind a 'ci:full-eval' label?
Aisha Raman: Done — full-mode requires the label. Default stays sampled 250 prompts in PR runs.
Liam O'Connor: Report HTML looks useful. Can we include a small visualization of embedding-distance distributions to help triage?
Aisha Raman: Added a small histogram and top-10 table in the report generator.
ci_summary: tokenization-robustness (GitHub Actions) — passed; unit tests passed; integration smoke passed; lint passed; 1 rerun of report generation job due to transient artifact upload failure.
notes_for_oncall: If this gate begins failing frequently after tokenizer upgrades, mark the prompt-set as 'skip_tokenization_gate' in tokenization_gate.yaml as a temporary mitigation and file ENG-XXXX to investigate tokenizer compatibility.

Ops: add dashboard for tokenization_gate failure rate by prompt-set
Docs: short runbook for triaging tokenization failures
